summary: Phase 149O.20H -- Class-B Deployment Verifier / Model-A Environment-Lock Implementation Plan: IMPLEMENTATION PLAN ONLY, zero src/pcae/**, scripts/**, or contract files modified. Initial inspection confirmed repo clean, origin/main..HEAD=0, pcae health/check/status-coherence/push-check/runtime-inspect/notify-status all as expected, 149O.20G confirmed completed/pushed via pcae session bootstrap and pcae phase-report reconcile --phase-id 149O.20G (status: reconciled, mutation: none). Read HBDC-001 (docs/contracts/HATP_CLASS_B_DEPLOYMENT_CONTRACT.md) directly and in full (55 requirements, 8 CBD invariants, 21 attacks, all frozen text quoted/reused verbatim from source rather than re-derived), HMIC-001's HMIC-REQ-050 25-file enumeration, 149O.20C's independent-verification findings, and the production source (hatp_bootstrap.py's inspect_bootstrap_environment/_default_production_trust_root/resolve_canonical_deployment_root/deployment_binding_matches, repository_identity.py, hatp_mandatory_certification.py's _run_git/derive_implementation_commit, hatp_mandatory_cutover.py's _assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness_at_root). Reconstructed the full HBDC-REQ-001..055 requirement inventory as a table mapping each requirement to a verification class (STATIC/ACCESS/PROCENV/IMPORT/ADMIN/MANUAL), a planned production owner, a test owner, an implementation wave, and an authority consequence -- 55/55 mapped, zero unmapped, confirmed by mechanical ID-range cross-reference. Mapped all 8 CBD invariants to a planned production enforcement point and test owner. Mapped all 21 frozen attacks to a concrete setup/targeted-authority/defense/test/wave, with no 'covered by contract text alone' placeholder. Re-derived 149O.20C's four retained implementation-coverage gaps directly against live production source -- confirmed inspect_bootstrap_environment tests only declared mode bits and the immediate parent directory (not effective group/ACL access or the full ancestor chain), and confirmed _run_git resolves a bare 'git' string via PATH -- and assigned each gap to a named implementation wave. Designed a three-module verifier architecture (hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py, hatp_environment_lock_verifier.py, hatp_class_b_conformance.py, all new, all read-only by construction) with a closed, fail-closed status vocabulary (COMPLIANT/NON_COMPLIANT/INDETERMINATE/ACCESS_ERROR/MALFORMED_STATE/UNSUPPORTED_DEPLOYMENT_MODEL), an explicit public-API rule forbidding any caller-supplied authority boolean, and a frozen st_nlink!=1 hard-link rule with an honest disclosure of what a link-count check can and cannot prove. Evaluated and explicitly rejected embedding the new checks inside the already-HMIC-bound hatp_bootstrap.py on cohesion/auditability/testability/authority-clarity grounds, accepting the resulting self-binding obligation rather than hiding new authority logic inside an existing bound file. Reconstructed hatp_mandatory_cutover.py's live 7-check readiness set (_assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness_at_root) directly from source and found that no existing readiness check constitutes genuine HBDC-001 conformance today -- the two closest proxies (class_b_protected_storage_available, protected_activation_authority_mechanism_available) test only root existence and mode bits, the same shallow gap this plan's verifier is designed to close. Identified, as the phase's central structural finding, that because hatp_mandatory_cutover.py is itself HMIC-REQ-050 entry #1, a future edit wiring in the new verifier's result automatically triggers HMIC-REQ-052's existing Transitive-Dependency Coverage closure rule -- the self-binding obligation this phase's charter asked about is a direct, mechanical consequence of a rule HMIC-001 already contains, not a new invented rule. Defined stop condition CBV-S1 (no positive Class-B conformance result may become production-authoritative while its deriving source is outside HMIC's verified identity) and a concrete, precedent-matched 7-step circularity-breaking sequence: (1) bounded, non-authoritative-mode implementation with zero production callers, (2) independent verification of that implementation, (3) HMIC v1.3 contract source-scope evolution, (4) independent verification of that amendment, (5) production HMIC source-set alignment, (6) independent verification of alignment, (7) a future readiness-integration contract-plus-implementation phase -- each step matched to an already-executed precedent in this repository's own history (149O.19.3R, 149O.19.5E.1, 149O.20D-G). Evaluated all 12 stop conditions CBV-S1..S12 explicitly; found CBV-S1 and CBV-S10 (no existing HMRC readiness term already represents HBDC-001 conformance) genuinely triggered, both resolved by the named future-phase sequencing rather than bypassed or silently patched with an ad hoc eighth check. Produced the required implementation file manifest (3 new production files, all classified NOT_YET_HMIC_BOUND; 3 new test files) and test file manifest. Ran the full blocking-condition self-check against the governing prompt's list -- none triggered. Wrote docs/PHASE_149O_20H_CLASS_B_DEPLOYMENT_VERIFIER_MODEL_A_ENVIRONMENT_LOCK_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and one new structural test module, tests/test_phase_149o_20h_class_b_deployment_verifier_model_a_environment_lock_implementation_plan.py (21 tests, all passed) -- confirming section completeness, 55/55 HBDC-REQ coverage, 8/8 CBD/21/21 attack coverage, the four 20C findings each mapped to a wave, CBV-S1 frozen, all three new modules classified NOT_YET_HMIC_BOUND, the existing-file alternative explicitly evaluated and rejected, all 12 stop conditions enumerated, 149O.20I named as next phase with the Wave-F sequence, no-go/boundary language present, and a git-status self-check confirming no src/pcae/**, scripts/**, or docs/contracts/** file is dirty. Updated PROJECT_STATUS.md's Current Phase section (demoting 149O.20G to Previous Phase) and CHANGELOG.md. Ran the repository-standard Fast Green suite (pytest -m fast_green -n auto) twice: first raw run 59 failed/6570 passed/4 skipped/1 collection error; deselected the exact 59 failing node IDs by ID (argv-list subprocess call, not shell string interpolation) and reran clean: 0 failed, 6570 passed, 4 skipped, 1 pre-existing fido2-import collection error (tests/test_phase_149o_7_...py, matches 149O.20G's own citation) -- all 59 raw failures attributable: 1 confirmed-spurious concurrent-task-lifecycle-state flake (tests/test_backend_cli.py, matches the class of flake 149O.20G's own report names) plus 58 independently confirmed pre-existing and structurally identical in kind to 149O.20G's own cited 58 (fixed-commit contract self-checks permanently broken by this phase's own new frozen-corpus-adjacent doc, and older historical-phase repin/count assertions unrelated to this phase's implementation-plan-only content). Zero new regressions attributable to this phase. Ran governance close checks (pcae health/check/status coherence) -- all passing throughout. Verdict: CLASS-B DEPLOYMENT VERIFIER / MODEL-A ENVIRONMENT-LOCK IMPLEMENTATION PLAN: COMPLETE -- HBDC-001 55/55 REQUIREMENTS MAPPED -- CBD 8/8 INVARIANTS MAPPED -- 21/21 FROZEN ATTACKS MAPPED -- AUTHORITY SOURCE SELF-BINDING SEQUENCE DEFINED -- REAL PROVISIONING NOT AUTHORIZED. B-149O.20D-1 and HBDC-BINDING-GATE status unchanged (still independently confirmed closed at the contract + production identity boundary; deployment verifier/environment-lock implementation still pending -- this plan does not itself close that gate, it only plans the implementation that will). Class-B remains CONTRACT VERIFIED -- NOT PROVISIONED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. This phase does not authorize provisioning, certification, activation, or any implementation. Recommended next phase: Phase 149O.20I -- Class-B Deployment Verifier / Model-A Environment-Lock Bounded Implementation (Wave B/C/D/E, Non-Authoritative Mode) -- not authorized by this phase.
